purpose: Apply the closed pure-wire codemod order. Only the named event module is writable. Independent private assays are withheld. No tools, shell, new files or unrelated changes.

---
title: Canonical unique journal command and retained-record laws
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: fabrication specification
status: closed pure-wire order; storage, authority and application acceptance excluded
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-journal-admission-lld.md
derived-from-sha256: 0ce36f3f5d8bbe4b79660d4d9ee8cda94f9861494fc2831c79441e66d283ab0a
---

## Receiving effect and selected realization

L-J01–L-J06 need one reusable transformation between a bounded command, its stable slot/content identities, and an exactly verifiable journal record. Preserve the existing artifact identity, typed witness construction and EAVT row laws. Extend their existing pure `journal/event.mjs` module with the three functions below; do not introduce an application codec, serializer, store, queue, provider adapter or new package. These are Code/Data laws with no filesystem, networking, clock or credential effects. They make no authority or storage decision. The existing module is admitted as placement of witness laws, not as design authority for their behavior.

The ordinary journal exports retain witness identities, core/observation values, verified source bodies and admission behavior; F-U07 removes locale dependence from source ordering and preserves historical permutations. Existing parseJournalWitness remains available with the source-set compatibility refinement in F-U07; the new record verifier applies its own exact correspondence rather than weakening the new contract to fit old permissiveness. Nothing in this order enables the journal's unique-admission API or grants dispatch permission. L-J07–L-J09 and effect-domain validation remain independent necessary integrations.

## Exported functions

**F-U01 — Address a command.** Add `addressUniqueJournalCommand(value, journalIdentity)`. It returns exactly `{command,commandRef,slotDigest}`, a deeply frozen JSON snapshot: `command` is an admitted copy of the caller value, commandRef uses addressArtifact, and slotDigest uses L-J02's exact tuple. Every identifier, closed object, domain/key correspondence, reference syntax, reference order, JSON resource bound and predecessor-in-causes condition in L-J01 is enforced. The journalIdentity argument is a nonempty string of at most 512 Unicode scalar values, rejecting unpaired surrogates. It is supplied by the trusted service caller; this function cannot prove that a deployment admits it. Effect-key journal must equal it. There is no parsing of paths or normalization of identifiers.

`value` inside the command is generic bounded JSON here; the domain validator is responsible for its interpretation. In particular, `value.approved = true`, a model-generated role or a syntactically valid grant reference confers no authority. This pure function neither invokes a validator callback nor claims to have checked a grant.

**F-U02 — Build a retained record.** Add `uniqueJournalRecord(command, options)`. Options is a closed object containing exactly `journal`, `seat`, `admittedAt`, and `artifacts`, all required. Journal and seat obey the identifier bound. admittedAt is a real timestamp whose round trip through the existing JavaScript date representation equals the original 24-character UTC-millisecond text; reject alternative offsets, normalized invalid dates and extended years. The interaction seat must equal command.key.principal. Use F-U01 to admit the command and compute its identity.

Construct the exact observation with fields `kind`, `seat`, `claim`, `address`, `time`, `causes`, `payload`, and `referencedArtifacts`, including the last array even when empty. Its kind is metroplat.journal.observation; payload is `[command.subject,"metroplat.journal.unique-admission",command,admittedAt]`; claim is `tm.mark("metroplat.journal.unique-admission")`; address is `tm.mark(eavtKey(payload))`; causes and referencedArtifacts are the command arrays. Use journalWitness, with F-U07's source ordering, for the existing witness construction; do not reimplement its six source artifacts, articulation, core identity or boundary record.

Options.artifacts is the L-J05 external artifact array in strictly increasing ordinal reference order, with exactly the required external set after subtracting verified witness-source references. Do not silently sort, deduplicate or ignore supplied entries. Each entry is closed `{ref,canonicalText}`; canonicalText must equal the canonical text returned by verifyArtifact for that reference. Additional, repeated, missing, noncanonical or mismatched bodies refuse.

Return exactly the L-J05 envelope `{kind,version,journal,commandRef,witness,artifacts}`, deeply frozen and independent of caller-owned mutable objects. Apply the specified JSON resource envelope to the whole constructed retained record as well as its parts. Do not return file bytes, an admission disposition, durability receipt or created flag. This is construction of an unpersisted value.

**F-U03 — Verify a retained record.** Add `parseUniqueJournalRecord(value, journalIdentity, expectedSlotDigest)`. All three arguments are required. expectedSlotDigest is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters supplied by the source locator. Apply bounded JSON admission before copying/hashing. The record must have exactly L-J05's six envelope fields, correct literals and configured journal, and no inherited or extra semantic properties admitted by the JSON contract.

Recover the command only from the witness observation's four-element EAVT payload. Verify expected subject, attribute and time correspondence by reconstructing the entire record through F-U02 from that command, record journal, observation seat/time and artifacts. Compare canonical JSON of the supplied record to canonical JSON of that reconstruction. This exact comparison rejects additional witness/observation fields, altered claim/address, fabricated core/sources, mismatched original time, altered reference arrays, omitted empty referencedArtifacts, or changed commandRef. Calling parseJournalWitness alone is insufficient. The exact reconstructed slot digest must equal expectedSlotDigest.

Return exactly `{record,command,slotDigest,reference}` as a deeply frozen snapshot, with reference exactly `{journal,subject,event,payload}` from L-J06. event is the verified original witness ID, payload the commandRef, and subject the original command subject. Different observation times for identical commands produce the same commandRef and slotDigest but normally different witness IDs; the persistence boundary must select the first record and return that original reference. This parser must not choose a winner or infer which call created it.

## Refusal, ownership and dependencies

**F-U04 — Stable refusal surface.** New exports throw TypeError with `code: "unique-journal-invalid"` for invalid input and a bounded diagnostic message naming the failed field or constraint. Do not echo arbitrary command content, artifact bodies or secrets. Known JSON/canonicalization and artifact-validation errors must be wrapped in this new refusal code; do not catch and turn unrelated programming failures into success. There is no unavailable result in a pure codec; the System boundary maps real storage failures to L-J06 separately. No caller object is mutated, including on refusal. Do not invoke getters or custom toJSON as a convenience for accepting non-JSON values; use the existing bounded JSON admission contract, which determines admissible runtime representations. Hostile JavaScript proxies are not a supported network input representation: the network boundary supplies values parsed from bounded JSON, not live caller-owned executable objects. This order does not claim that ordinary JavaScript reflection can inspect arbitrary proxies without invoking their traps.

All returned JSON containers, including nested command value, witness observation/core/sources and external artifact entries, are frozen snapshots. Reusing an immutable shared primitive is permitted; retaining a mutable caller container is not. Returned canonical values must remain byte-identical if the caller later mutates any input object.

**F-U05 — Reuse and exact placement.** Writable input is only `code/src/semiotic-eavt/journal/event.mjs`, SHA-256 `69160a522e6f7f9319a6e4743d8940ef2cac00c44150591b845c992c594f1833`. Extend its existing exports; the package already exposes the event module and no new export-map entry is needed. Allowed added dependencies are Node's `createHash` from node:crypto (pure hashing), existing JSON canonicalization/admission/resource-envelope exports, existing artifact address/verification/reference predicates, `tm` from the existing semiotic-expression-notation export, and eavtKey from the existing EAVT row export. The current imports of journal witness laws remain. The only changes to existing exported behavior are the source-order construction and source-set verification in F-U07; all unrelated behavior remains. No System dependency or physical I/O may be added to Code.

The source provider receives the exact target plus read-only source/API evidence for reused dependencies. If that evidence shows an assumed API absent or inconsistent with the order, refuse rather than implement a replacement. The literal resource bounds pinned in L-J01 govern v1; verify the imported JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE matches them and refuse an unsupported changed envelope instead of silently changing wire behavior.

Use the existing fabrication LLD's closed exact-substring codemod result. Clause references are F-U01–F-U07; edits to read-only inputs, unrelated exports, tests or new files refuse materialization. Capture all dependency input digests and recheck them along with target and governing specifications before promotion. No schema/code artifact generated by this order substitutes for domain authority validation.

**F-U06 — Independent receiving observations.** Before invoking the source provider, commit private assays against the exact order. Use existing independent artifact/witness/EAVT laws to compute expected identities, not the new functions themselves as their oracle. Include both domains; nonnull predecessor correspondence; distinct domain/journal/key identities; same command across two boundary times; changed value with unchanged slot but changed content identity; original-reference verification; artifact-set subtraction, canonical text and exact body verification; unknown fields and altered witness components; invalid or unpaired Unicode and normalization distinctions; invalid date normalization; wrong journal/slot/principal; aggregate bounds; mutation after construction; and refusal before any host effect. Exercise ordinary journalWitness/parseJournalWitness compatibility separately, including reversed historical source arrays and explicit rejection of duplicate, missing, surplus or altered source entries. Demonstrate new source-array ordering independent of locale-sensitive comparison, and retain each historical witness ID, core, observation and verified body. The known spread of the observation in journalWitness retains an explicitly supplied empty referencedArtifacts array; include this established correspondence in acceptance rather than inventing a wrapper for a removal that does not occur.

Reject a candidate if any required pure law fails; a revised candidate must come from a fresh source derivation with admitted public feedback. Keep private assays withheld. Preserve the full predecessor chain, invocation/environment/candidate digests and limits. Successful receiving proves these pure wire transformations only: no storage durability, conflict winner, sender exclusion, authorization, connected service or assistant effect has been demonstrated.

**F-U07 — Source order is representation, not authority.** Change journalWitness's source-array sort from localeCompare to ordinal reference comparison (the valid references are ASCII, so ordinary code-unit order suffices). This must not change any artifact's canonical body/reference, witness core, witness ID, boundary observation, causes, or the existing handling of optional observation fields. Only the array representation order changes.

Refine parseJournalWitness to compare its supplied source array as an exact set of reference/body pairs against the newly reconstructed expected array. Require an array of exactly the expected length, each entry with exactly ref and canonicalText, each reference occurring once, and every pair matching the reconstructed reference/body. Reject extra entry fields, wrong types, duplicate references, missing or surplus sources, changed canonical text and invented identities. Do not silently discard duplicates or accept merely content-equivalent noncanonical source text. Keep its existing checks of witness kind, ID, bytes, core and reconstructed observation. Return the reconstructed witness in canonical ordinal source order. Older ordinary witnesses in another source-array order remain readable without rewriting retained source files or readdressing the witness.

New unique-record parsing remains stricter than historical ordinary witness parsing: F-U03's whole-record reconstruction requires the canonical source order inside a version-1 unique record. Historical compatibility of ordinary source arrays is not permission to silently normalize a noncanonical new unique record. The record source and its exact canonical bytes remain independently verifiable.

## Existing-law observation and review limits

A [controlled observation](evidence/2026-09-27-journal-unique-wire/observation.json) used the current artifact, EAVT and journal-witness functions on one fixture command at two dates. Command content identity and slot identity remained stable; observation witness identities differed; each witness round-tripped through the current parser. The explicitly supplied empty observation referencedArtifacts array survived, while the core retained its own boundary artifact. This falsified a review concern that journalWitness would remove that explicit empty field. It does not exercise the future three exports or the domain message schema.

The source-order change addresses the dependency on locale-sensitive comparison visible in the existing constructor and exact-source-array comparison visible in the parser. No cross-locale production failure was observed here. Its acceptance requires the independent F-U06 observations, including historical source permutations; neither this diagnostic nor a reviewer assertion supplies that acceptance.

realizationContract.text:
---
title: Bounded source derivation and independent assessment for muse-assist
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: specification
status: derived LLD; operator-mediated realization using existing tools
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-hld.md
derived-from-sha256: 5f824fb118e4cdfec8e23cc2f74e8aff667eff420d5e461ffb4c60b8ad57c6e9
---

## What this is

This LLD closes H-F2/H-F3's first source-derivation realization using existing inference and isolation tools, without adding a scheduler, gateway, generator framework, or application-specific fabricator. It governs an operator-mediated transformation from a closed fabrication order into a staged candidate and separately held acceptance evidence. It is a bounded first realization, not automation of the whole Customer Demand-to-code chain.

## Work-order and candidate carriers

**L-F01.** The admitted generation input MUST bind the predecessor chain, fabrication order, current transformation-input bytes/digests, public examples, output contract, model/configuration and invocation bounds. The input MUST exclude private assay source, fixtures, expected results and assessor conversation. A separate assessor MUST derive and commit the private assay inventory before source derivation starts. Commitment is a byte digest, not proof that the assay is sufficient.

**L-F02.** The first output contract is a closed JSON object with `disposition` (`candidate` or `refused`), `reason`, and `edits`. A refused result MUST have no edits and a specific reason. Each candidate edit MUST contain exactly `path`, `inputSha256`, `before`, `after`, and `clauses`. `path` identifies an admitted relative source file, `inputSha256` binds its original bytes, `before` is a nonempty exact substring occurring once at the point of application, `after` is replacement text, and `clauses` is a nonempty array of governing clause IDs. Multiple edits to a file apply in output order against one original input digest. Missing files, ambiguous text matches, path escape, mismatched input digest, unrecognized clause IDs, or extra object fields MUST refuse materialization. Candidate outputs are untrusted source until independently assessed.

The deterministic materializer applies only admitted textual replacements to a staged copy and computes full resulting file digests. This is a bounded codemod application, not behavioral source derivation. It MUST NOT execute generator-provided shell commands. New files require a separately specified creation contract; this first work order uses existing files. Actual transformed bytes, input/output digests and clause correspondence become the source-result evidence required by H-F2/F-H07.

## Generator access boundary

**L-F03.** The source provider MUST run in a fresh inference context with no inherited conversation, no assessor material, and no shared-checkout write access. For the first local realization, the existing Codex executable MAY be invoked noninteractively with the requested GPT-6 Luna model inside a Bubblewrap mount/PID namespace. The only task content is the public input packet delivered on standard input. The host checkout, assay directory, host process namespace, session history, user/project configuration, skills and connectors MUST NOT be mounted or otherwise supplied. The public output schema MAY be mounted read-only. Runtime libraries, TLS/DNS files and the existing authentication file may be made available solely to run the authenticated provider; authentication material MUST NOT be printed or placed in prompts.

The invocation MUST use a fresh ephemeral session, ignore user configuration and rules, disable shell, web search, apps and further agent delegation where the installed CLI supports those controls, and use a read-only model-command sandbox. External process isolation supplies the filesystem boundary; prompts and the CLI's read-only setting alone do not. Native tools which remain advertised cannot see the omitted mounts. The invocation MUST NOT resume this conversation or any previous source/assessor session. The actual argument vector, executable digest/version, public input digest, observed model and event record MUST be retained without credentials. Undeclared tool use, unexpected mounts, source input change, unavailable authentication/model, or source-provider access to assessor material MUST reject that invocation. No alternate model is silently substituted.

**L-F04.** Before live source generation, a deterministic process under the same mount profile MUST establish that the host checkout and an external sentinel cannot be read, that the process view is namespaced, and that only the intended task inputs are available. This demonstrates the local process boundary, not provider-server confidentiality or model correctness. The provider's own server retention/isolation remains a trust assumption and MUST be stated. The operator MUST NOT send private assay content through feedback, diagnostics or a resumed source session.

## Independent assessment and promotion

**L-F05.** The assessor MUST run the committed assays against the content-bound candidate, separately from the source provider. Executing candidate code MUST not give it a communication channel back to that provider or access to operational credentials/private user data. A network-denied execution namespace with only required runtime, dependency, candidate and assay inputs is the selected local assessment boundary. The assessor may inspect private results; the source generator receives only a separately admitted public reproduction or changed specification, never private fixtures or raw assay logs.

**L-F06.** The evidence bundle MUST contain specification/chain/input/candidate/assay digests, provider/model/configuration, invocation boundaries, method, environment, assessor, result, limits, and measured token/time/cost information where available. Missing cash-cost data MUST be marked unavailable rather than zero. Generic artifact receipts may reference this bundle by locator/digest; receipts do not prove acceptance. Failed candidates remain rejected. New evidence or revised specifications can justify a new candidate; an invisible edit after a failed assay cannot.

**L-F07.** Promotion MUST compare each original input digest with current shared-checkout bytes immediately before applying the accepted replacements. Any mismatch refuses the entire promotion batch and preserves both candidate and concurrent edits. All affected files must pass this check before any is replaced. Promotion MUST retain the accepted output digest and actual receiving-workflow evidence; staging checks do not establish public deployment or assistant operation.

## Implementations

The installed host currently has Bubblewrap and Codex CLI 0.154.0. A preliminary empty namespace probe could not see `/home/emsenn/info`; the complete invocation profile still requires L-F04's recorded check. The CLI's local help exposes ephemeral, ignored-user-config, output-schema and noninteractive execution. [Official configuration documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) defines the shell-tool switch; [noninteractive documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) describes the ephemeral invocation. These are invocation capabilities, not proof of assay independence or generated-code correctness.

The separately inspected ops inference route reported one configured `llama3.2:3b` provider with no admitted resource-availability observation. It was not invoked or substituted for the requested Luna source role. Its existence is not evidence of available capacity. The local invocation above uses existing tooling; no inference service is being repaired or reimplemented here.

## Open questions

- **L-FO1:** The first source invocation must establish actual model/authentication availability and record L-F04's complete boundary check. Failure preserves the closed order and assays; it does not authorize direct hand coding.
- **L-FO2:** Broader unattended generation, scheduler integration and automatic demand-to-design derivation are not supplied by this operator-mediated protocol. Any subsequent automation must preserve these contracts and receive its own specification before implementation.

domainContract.text:
---
title: Unique journal commands, references and causal recovery for muse-assist
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: specification
status: derived LLD; wire contract refined; storage and domain integration not yet accepted
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-shared-effect-lld.md
derived-from-sha256: 0a5a8b72a9833a64c8b721d02619fe0de9959d557fe993d0ef6c0c6216359721
---

## Receiving effect and dependency order

This refines L-E01–L-E04 and L-E08, including L-I02's request replay and L-W02's stable references. A caller can retry an admitted command and recover its original reference; competing workers cannot each acquire the right associated with the same effect successor; ordinary journal queries retain these facts across dates and restart. The carrier is the owning causal journal. Retain existing witness identities, causal/source validation, and useful feed/subject projections. Do not introduce a Muse-owned record authority or treat an invocation receipt as effect reservation.

The command/envelope laws belong to the Code layer and use Data's canonical JSON/content identity. Physical source retention, durable publication, recovery, discovery and compaction belong to Systems. The current location of a filesystem implementation inside the Code package is migration evidence, not a license for a new upward dependency from Code to Systems. Fabrication must place new physical persistence in the shared journal's System implementation and account for existing direct readers/writers of the same carrier.

## Closed command and identity contract

**L-J01 — Semantic command.** The canonical command is a closed JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `domain`, `key`, `subject`, `value`, `causes`, and `artifactRefs`. `kind` is `metroplat.journal.unique-command`; `version` is integer 1. `domain` is `interaction` or `effect-successor`. `subject` is the exact journal subject, a nonempty string of at most 512 Unicode scalar values. `value` is a JSON value validated by the domain contract before admission. JSON values must satisfy the repository's existing JSON admission/canonicalization contract; nonfinite numbers, undefined values and non-JSON values refuse. Admission uses the existing `JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE` for the whole command and, separately, the whole retained envelope: 1,048,576 source/canonical UTF-8 bytes, depth 64, 100,000 nodes, 4,096 members per object, 65,536 elements per array, 262,144 UTF-8 bytes per string, and 1,024 bytes per key. The 512-scalar identifier bound additionally applies. Reject unpaired surrogates rather than replacing them or normalizing identifiers. No Unicode normalization, trimming or case folding changes identity. Boundary transport size limits precede parsing; bounded JSON admission precedes canonicalization/hashing. A valid command whose complete retained envelope exceeds the bound is refused before publication; it is not silently truncated. A changed resource envelope requires a versioned contract revision, not an environment-dependent interpretation of version 1.

For `interaction`, `key` is a closed object containing exactly nonempty bounded strings `context`, `principal`, and `requestId`. For `effect-successor`, `key` contains exactly `journal`, `effectId`, and `predecessor`; journal/effectId are nonempty bounded strings and predecessor is null or an exact existing witness content reference. Each bounded key string has the same 512-scalar maximum. `journal` must equal the deployment-bound owning journal identity. Context/principal bindings come from authenticated interaction admission; a generic command parser does not establish them.

`causes` and `artifactRefs` are arrays of unique valid artifact references, sorted by ordinal code-point order for canonical representation. Reject duplicates and noncanonical order rather than silently changing a signed or compared command. An effect command with nonnull predecessor must include that exact reference in causes. The explicit null predecessor denotes initial admission, never a recovery shortcut. The effect-transition validator independently determines whether this predecessor and command are lawful; generic journal admission is not that validator.

**L-J02 — Stable bytes.** Encode the closed command with the existing `canonicalJson` implementation, UTF-8, without a trailing newline. Its content identity is the existing `addressArtifact(command).ref`, verified using the matching existing artifact verifier. Do not introduce a second JSON serializer or ad hoc digest format. Observation time, worker invocation/attempt identity outside the domain value, boundary caller metadata, local root path and retry arrival time are not automatically added to these semantic bytes.

The unique slot digest is lower-case SHA-256 hex of canonical UTF-8 JSON for `["metroplat.journal.unique-slot",1,journalIdentity,command.domain,command.key]`. `journalIdentity` is operator-bound service identity, never a filesystem path or a caller-selected substitution. Hashing this typed tuple avoids delimiter/path ambiguity. Neither command content nor observation time is in the slot key: changed content must conflict at the same occupied key. These digests are internal storage identifiers, not grants or unguessable access tokens.

**L-J03 — Same command versus new observation.** Canonically identical commands at one slot return the first admitted witness and original observation time. A subsequent boundary time cannot create another record or change the returned identity. Any canonical command change at that slot is a conflict, even if the new command appears preferable or the old grant has expired. Authorization to resolve an existing record is rechecked; knowing a retry identifier cannot reveal another context's input. A conflict in effect succession causes the regulator to read and validate the occupied successor; it does not license overwriting it or selecting an unrelated predecessor.

## One retained journal fact

**L-J04 — Witness correspondence.** The existing journal witness representation is retained. The admission observation's payload is the ordinary EAVT row `[command.subject,"metroplat.journal.unique-admission",command,admittedAt]`. Its claim is the existing typed mark `metroplat.journal.unique-admission`; its address is `tm.mark(eavtKey(row))`, using the existing typed-term constructor rather than passing the key string as a term. Its causes equal command.causes; its referencedArtifacts equal command.artifactRefs; its observation seat is the admitted caller. `causes` and `referencedArtifacts` here describe the observation: the witness constructor additionally includes its own boundary artifact in the witness core, which must not be stripped to force core-level equality. Construct and verify the witness with the existing journal-witness/artifact laws; do not accept a caller's alleged witness ID without that verification.

`admittedAt` is a boundary-generated UTC timestamp in exact `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ` form representing a real instant. It is retained with the first admission and excluded from the semantic command comparison. The caller is a nonempty authenticated principal identifier bounded to 512 Unicode scalar values and supplied by the trusted boundary. For an interaction witness, the admitted caller equals command.key.principal; a worker service cannot replace that authenticated origin with its own identifier. Neither caller nor time is inferred from model text. Newly constructed witness source arrays use ordinal reference order, independent of the process locale. Verification of an older ordinary witness may accept a permutation of the same exact verified source set without changing its witness ID, core, observation or source bodies. Missing, duplicate, surplus or changed sources still refuse. A new version-1 unique record uses the canonical order; historical ordinary source bytes do not need rewriting to recover their capability.

**L-J05 — Retained record.** The immutable source envelope is a closed object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `journal`, `commandRef`, `witness`, and `artifacts`. `kind` is `metroplat.journal.unique-record`; version is 1; journal is the configured identity; commandRef is L-J02's content reference; witness is L-J04's verified witness. Artifacts is a reference-sorted array of closed `{ref,canonicalText}` objects. Its reference set is exactly `command.artifactRefs` minus the reference set in the verified witness's own sources. Each remaining reference occurs once, with independently verified canonical JSON text, byte-equal to `verifyArtifact(ref, canonicalText).canonical.text`; alternate whitespace/encodings refuse. Each subtracted reference must resolve to its verified witness source body. References already present in those sources must not be repeated in artifacts. Missing, surplus, wrong-address or contradictory content refuses publication.

Recover the command, slot digest, subject, caller and time from the verified witness and configured identity. Do not maintain independently editable copies of those values in the envelope. Store canonical envelope JSON plus one final newline. The root-relative source path is `unique-admissions/v1/<slotDigest>.json` beneath the existing owning journal directory. Neither subject, principal, request text nor effect ID appears directly in that pathname. Staging files are never admitted sources. Use L-E03's durable create-only publication; verify envelope canonical bytes and filename correspondence on resolution.

**L-J06 — References and results.** A successful receipt returns the immutable reference `{journal,subject,event,payload}`: journal is the configured service identity, subject the exact command subject, event the existing witness ID, and payload the canonical command's content reference. No local file path is a public locator. This is a concrete L-W02 reference; resolution verifies all four fields and the expected unique-admission kind.

Admission returns a closed tagged result: `{disposition:"created",reference}`, `{disposition:"existing",reference}`, `{disposition:"conflict",reference}`, or `{disposition:"unavailable",reason}`. Reason is exactly one of `storage-unavailable`, `storage-unsupported`, `source-corrupt`, `evidence-unavailable`, `resource-limit`, `maintenance-busy`, or `publication-uncertain`. Unsupported storage semantics use storage-unsupported; malformed or wrong-address retained bytes use source-corrupt; an unresolved required reference uses evidence-unavailable; exhausted bounded traversal uses resource-limit; failure to acquire required maintenance protection uses maintenance-busy; a failure after publication may have become visible uses publication-uncertain; other host I/O failure uses storage-unavailable. Classification must never assert that a failed publication did not occur. Private diagnostic evidence is retained by the boundary; raw paths, credentials and exception strings are not public reasons. Invalid command/identity/authority is refused before storage; it must not be mislabeled unavailable. A denied caller receives no occupied reference. Only a verified successful publisher can receive created. Existing/conflict are returned only after verifying and completing both the occupied source's and its required closure's durability boundaries under L-J07; they never transfer dispatch rights. Any uncertain publication, corrupt source or unresolvable required evidence yields unavailable and cannot be translated to absence.

The public resolution outcomes remain L-W02's resolved/unavailable/forbidden/invalid distinctions. Absence of a slot can be used only by the local create-only admission operation after authenticating the context; a remote query cannot turn an unavailable record into a new initial effect.

## Causal retention and recovery

**L-J07 — Required closure before acknowledgment.** Before acknowledging created, existing or conflict, establish durable retention of the witness's complete required causal/artifact closure, including earlier request, assignment, proposal and authority evidence used by its domain contract. Verifying that bytes can currently be read is insufficient: their source files may not yet be synchronized. The retained record carries its direct external artifact bodies; predecessor witnesses and their source bodies must remain durably resolvable in the same owning journal or an explicitly admitted durable external custody service. Resolve cycles, missing causes, incorrect digests and resource-limit overflow as refusal/unavailable; never truncate the required closure or call a Boolean supplied by inference proof of persistence.

The System persistence implementation must expose a real durability barrier over the required retained source set and its directory entries, and return evidence identifying the content protected by that barrier. For an occupied slot, resolve the stored command's closure, not the rejected caller's alternative command. An existing reader must synchronize the source file and every ancestor directory through the filesystem root, because it cannot infer which ancestor creations an interrupted publisher synchronized. A verified deployment initialization barrier may discharge ancestors above the journal only if that exact root binding remains valid; merely observing that a directory exists cannot. The barrier protects the exact content references verified during this call; a generic success flag or a receipt for another closure cannot discharge it. Deduplicate shared source files within one barrier. Ordinary segment files can contain more evidence than the selected closure; synchronizing a containing file is acceptable, but does not expand the caller's authority to read or disclose its other content. Existing already-durable unique records can satisfy predecessor custody without copying the whole ancestral chain into every child record. Do not create quadratic copies of causal history.

Destructive compaction/retention must preserve these identities and source availability: verify and durably publish replacement source content before removing the old representation, and protect unresolved work's required evidence from retention deletion. Admission and destructive maintenance must have an enforced ordering covering closure discovery, byte verification, source-file and directory synchronization, slot publication, and acknowledgment. Maintenance cannot delete or replace a source between discovery and acknowledgment. If another caller completes an interrupted slot, it acquires the same protection and repeats the unresolved closure barrier before acknowledging it. An immutable slot's existence alone is therefore insufficient to skip source retention. A comment, stale PID or caller assurance is insufficient. The exact host maintenance/barrier interface and its consumers must be closed in the storage fabrication order before this admission API is enabled. The accepted durable create-only helper supplies publication, not this whole-source barrier or maintenance exclusion.

**L-J08 — Source precedes index.** Reconstruct admission state from retained verified witness sources whenever a derived index is absent or incomplete. A present index file is not proof that it contains every published witness. Specifically, interruption after segment publication and before its admitted-index append must not make a retained predecessor appear unknown or leave its dependent permanently quarantined. Repair may append derived entries, but cannot invent source witnesses or accept an invalid causal closure. Reads of source and derived state must converge without manual deletion of indexes or restarting the entire service.

Distinguish the actual roles of the current `index/causal-admission/v2` files: the admitted lookup is derived from retained source segments; externally referenced artifact bodies and pending witness bodies may have no other current copy. Do not erase an entire directory merely because it is named index. Migration must retain those actual source bodies and their identity/causal properties before retiring the old representation.

**L-J09 — All relevant reads.** Extend exact artifact resolution, per-feed reads, row folds, as-of causal reads, subject/date/territory discovery, source-status queries and compaction to include unique admissions. Readers must deduplicate by verified witness ID when a source also has a normal segment projection. A normal segment copy cannot prove that the unique slot still exists; effect ownership and command replay resolve the authoritative slot directly.

A source-only admission must remain discoverable even if interruption prevented every optional projection/index write. Slot creation under an existing directory must invalidate any discovery cache that would hide it. Do not rely only on dated-directory timestamps, because the selected source namespace is date-independent. Date and subject filters use the verified first witness's time and exact subject, not pathname guesses. A request retried tomorrow resolves its original slot and reference. Unreadable/corrupt source or a resource limit must not be caught and returned as an empty feed, absent command, or permission to repeat work.

Derived lookup caches are permitted, but their invalidation and rebuild behavior must be demonstrated. The physical source-discovery strategy must bound reads and avoid re-verifying unrelated historical artifacts on every admission. This is an implementation obligation, not permission to hide undiscovered facts behind a resource limit. A limit produces an explicit unavailable result.

## Migration observations and required acceptance

A controlled [recovery observation](evidence/2026-09-27-journal-admission-recovery/observation.json) retained an admitted witness in its segment, removed only its derived admitted-index entry, cleared process caches, and submitted a dependent. The source witness remained readable, while its recovered admission state was absent and the dependent stayed quarantined. This is a constructed partial-index image corresponding to the source/index publication gap, not a simulated power outage. It establishes a missing recovery behavior that must be corrected before unique admission is treated as complete.

The affected current System consumers include `readEvents`, `eventFiles`, `scanSourceFilesInternal`, `listDailyFeedsAtDirectory`, `subjectLogPathsInternal`, `territoryLogPathsInternal`, `territoryStructuralSignature`, `readArtifactSource` and `compactJournalStore`, plus the public journal API. The current compact store supplies segment admission, causal state/artifact lookup and legacy compaction. Its direct semantic-record readers/writers are additional consumers of the same evidence family; they must not become an unverified bypass or force a new System dependency into Code.

Independent acceptance must demonstrate: same command/time-varied retries returning one original reference; changed-command conflict; two processes and two in-process workers with one created result; exact source/reference verification; cross-date/subject reads; restart with source publication but no projection; a partial existing admitted index; missing/corrupt cause retention; failed durability barrier; compaction while work remains unresolved; and explicit unavailable rather than empty reads. Exercise actual storage effects, not only the typed parser. Application acceptance additionally requires authenticated intake and effect dispatch through these contracts; this document and the lower publication primitive do not supply that complete workflow.

## Closed wire law and remaining fabrication boundary

The command, content identity, witness correspondence, immutable envelope and receipt shapes above are Code/Data laws. Their independent acceptance must include unchanged command identity across admission times, changed-content conflict, exact tuple domain separation, Unicode identifier distinctions, unknown-key refusal, malformed/noncanonical references, aggregate envelope overflow, and observation/core boundary-artifact correspondence. Those pure laws can be fabricated separately once their source placement and exact exported interfaces are specified. Passing those checks does not authorize storage admission or sending.

Physical integration remains a single dependent work family: source discovery and partial-index recovery, a real closure durability barrier ordered against destructive maintenance, ordinary and unique source readers, and authenticated domain admission. L-J07 does not select a host locking implementation by implication. The storage order must specify its mechanism and all destructive consumers before enabling this API. Domain-specific interaction payloads and effect-transition validation also remain required; a command with a syntactically valid `value` has no authority solely because the generic codec accepts it.
